question: What is a primary characteristic of operating room walls and floors?

options.A: Covered with textured fabric to absorb sound
options.B: Built using treated wooden panels for flexibility
options.C: Painted with high-gloss organic plant-based finishes
options.D: Constructed from non-porous and seamless materials

explanation: Non-porous and seamless surfaces prevent dust accumulation and withstand repeated chemical disinfection, which is vital for infection control. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why is the surgical suite typically located in a low-traffic area of the hospital?

options.A: To allow natural sunlight to illuminate the sterile instrument tables
options.B: To reduce ambient noise and lower the risk of airborne contamination
options.C: To keep surgical supplies closer to the central hospital pharmacy
options.D: To make it easier for visiting family members to access the recovery area

explanation: Isolating the OR suite away from general hospital traffic restricts the movement of dust and microbes into the sterile core. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h1)

question: In which zone of the operating theatre are staff permitted to wear ordinary street clothes?
explanation: The unrestricted zone acts as the outer gateway where street clothes are allowed before personnel transition into scrub attire. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following activities or areas belongs in the semi-restricted zone?

options.A: Direct scrubbing at sinks right before entering the theatre
options.B: Patient reception and administrative paperwork desks
options.D: Active surgical procedures involving open wounds

explanation: Service corridors, equipment storage, and instrument processing areas require scrub attire but not full sterile masking, placing them in the semi-restricted zone. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h2)

question: What type of air pressure is maintained inside the operating room relative to the outside corridors?
explanation: Positive room pressure forces air outward when doors open, preventing external dust and microbes from entering the surgical space. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary function of High-Efficiency Particulate Air (HEPA) filters in an HVAC system?

options.A: Regulating the speed at which air changes occur in the room
options.B: Warming the surgical suite during lengthy procedures
options.C: Removing microscopic particles and microorganisms from incoming air
options.D: Adjusting the humidity levels to prevent patient hypothermia

explanation: HEPA filtration traps tiny airborne particles and pathogens, ensuring that the air delivered into the surgical suite is ultra-clean. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of ceiling-mounted service booms in the operating room?

options.A: Eliminating the need for electrical safety checks
options.B: Eliminating tangled floor cords and tripping hazards
options.C: Providing natural lighting for delicate eye procedures
options.D: Reducing the cost of surgical gas maintenance

explanation: Ceiling booms suspend power cables and gas hoses above the floor, keeping walkways clear for rapid staff movement and equipment rolling. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why are cool-beam technology surgical lights used in modern operating theatres?

options.A: To reduce the overall electrical voltage consumption of the hospital
options.B: To illuminate deep surgical cavities without drying exposed patient tissues
options.C: To allow the surgical team to operate in total darkness
options.D: To prevent the operating table from overheating during long procedures

explanation: Surgical lamps generate intense illumination, and cool-beam technology prevents excessive thermal radiation from damaging or drying delicate open tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h4)

question: Where should scrubbed personnel keep their hands after performing a surgical hand scrub?

options.A: Resting directly on their surgical masks
options.B: Hanging loosely down near their knees
options.C: Above the waist and away from their clothing
options.D: Folded tightly against their trouser pockets

explanation: Keeping hands above the waist and away from non-sterile scrubs prevents accidental contamination of the sterile gown and gloves. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h5)

question: What should an unscrubbed team member do when moving near a sterile instrument table?

options.A: Maintain a safe distance of at least one foot and never reach across it
options.B: Touch the edges of the table to steady themselves in tight spaces
options.C: Wear sterile gloves just while handing items across the surface
options.D: Lean across the table as long as they do not touch the instruments

explanation: Unscrubbed personnel must respect the boundaries of sterile fields to avoid dropping unsterile particles or clothing onto sterile supplies. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h5)

question: Which three elements form the surgical fire triad present in many operating rooms?

options.D: Heat, cold air, and surgical instruments

explanation: A surgical fire requires an ignition source, an oxidizer like oxygen, and a fuel source such as skin prep or drapes to sustain combustion. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the purpose of scavenger systems in the operating room environment?

options.A: Clearing surgical smoke generated by electrosurgery
options.B: Suctioning blood and fluids directly from the surgical wound
options.C: Removing waste anesthetic gases to protect healthcare staff
options.D: Filtering dust particles from the air conditioning ducts

explanation: Scavenging systems capture and exhaust waste anesthetic gases safely outside the building, preventing chronic occupational exposure among OR personnel. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which perioperative nursing role operates primarily within the sterile field during a procedure?
explanation: The scrub nurse wears sterile gown and gloves, remaining within the sterile field to handle instruments and assist the surgical team directly. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h7)

question: Which of the following responsibilities belongs primarily to the circulating nurse?

options.A: Managing room traffic, documentation, and conducting safety counts
options.B: Closing the subcutaneous skin layers with absorbable sutures
options.C: Selecting and handing specialized clamps directly to the operating surgeon
options.D: Maintaining the sterility of instrument trays on the Mayo stand

explanation: The circulating nurse remains unscrubbed to document care, coordinate room activities, manage supplies, and participate in sponge and instrument counts. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h7)
